Choose it when rendering coherent ray packets, but avoid it when high-quality volume rendering requires deep subdivisions that exacerbate thread divergence [S9, unofficial].

The claim states that one should choose the method (implied to be the single-kernel/texture-based approach discussed in S9) for coherent ray packets, but avoid it for high-quality volume rendering with deep subdivisions due to thread divergence. Source S9 explicitly supports this: it recommends using a 2D grid/block to map neighboring threads (rays) for spatial coherence to improve cache hits (supporting the 'coherent ray packets' part). It also explicitly states that for volumetric ray tracing/high-quality volume rendering, deep subdivisions cause neighboring rays to diverge significantly, leading to SIMD stalls, which was a 'deal killer' issue. Thus, the evidence supports both the recommendation for coherent packets and the warning against it for high-quality volume rendering due to divergence.
supported

Choose it for GPU implementations requiring efficient random access to octree node data [S9, unofficial].

The claim states that the evidence supports choosing this method for GPU implementations requiring efficient random access to octree node data. Source [S9] explicitly recommends binding octree node data as a texture and reading it with `tex1Dfetch()` specifically 'since you will be accessing it randomly.' It further explains that texture memory is preferred over constant memory because constant memory is optimized for broadcast reads, whereas octree traversal involves random access patterns. Therefore, every fact in the claim is present in the evidence.
